description: Send a POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE request to any DocStar API endpoint for the signed-in user and return { status, ok, headers, data }. Use it for changes no dedicated tool covers, once you know the exact endpoint: from the quickstart-docstar skill's recipes, or looked up with get_docstar_api_docs. For GET requests use call_any_read_api_of_docstar. Never guess a URL. Pass the full url with path variables filled in, the method, the headers the endpoint's docs list, query params in `query` (not in the url) and the JSON body in `body`. Send the endpoint's auth header with an empty value "": the user's token is filled in automatically. Never put a token there yourself. Show the user what you're about to send and get a yes before any call that creates, changes, publishes or deletes something.

body.description: JSON request body, as the endpoint's docs show it. Leave it out when the endpoint takes no body.

headers.description: Request headers as name/value pairs, as the docs list them. Give the auth header (Authorization, proxy_auth_token, x-api-key, ...) an empty value "" so the signed-in user's token is filled in; never put a token here yourself. Pass {} when the endpoint needs no headers. Example: {"proxy_auth_token": "", "Content-Type": "application/json"}

method.description: HTTP method from the endpoint's docs

query.description: Query params as name/value pairs; an array sends the param once per item. Example: {"type": "flow", "bringflows": true}

url.description: Full endpoint URL with path variables replaced by real values, e.g. https://api.example.com/users/42. Put query params in `query`, not here.

name: call_any_api_of_docstar
